basis: SCSA Year 12 Human Biology ATAR syllabus for teaching from 2024, applicable in 2026
qualification: This is an independent teaching coverage map, not SCSA endorsement. Lesson explanations and worked examples support inquiry skills; they do not replace a teacher-supervised investigation or school assessment program. The separately published 2027 syllabus should be used when planning that teaching year.

themes.focus: How copying errors, division errors and mutagens change genetic material
How inherited differences and the environment affect expressed traits
Why mutation supplies new alleles for subsequent evolutionary change
Using allele frequencies to compare populations and generations
Distinguishing mutation, selection, drift and migration as causes of change
Explaining disease-allele patterns, including the sickle-cell example
Linking inheritance, competition, reproductive success and isolation to speciation
Explaining how PCR, gels and sequence information enable evolutionary comparisons
Comparing molecular evidence and explaining how new analyses revise relationships
Reading shared ancestry and alternative branching hypotheses
Explaining missing evidence through formation, preservation and discovery biases
Combining a relative sequence with numerical age constraints
Selecting and evaluating layer order, index fossils, carbon-14 and potassium-argon evidence
Comparing brain proportions, digits, locomotion, jaws and teeth among great apes
Comparing the seven specified fossil taxa using anatomy and other evidence
Comparing manufacture and materials across the four specified Homo tool cultures
Explaining testable questions, hypotheses and expected patterns
Explaining controls, sampling, safe methods and research ethics
Distinguishing valid measurement from repeatable results
Working with data patterns, measurement limits and sample size
Separating supported conclusions from assumptions and unsupported claims
Using labelled scientific representations and evidence-linked explanations
